parole.significato: amah, ayah; a native Indonesian woman employed as a wet nurse, nanny and/or maid by Europeans in the former Dutch East…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese ꦧꦧꦸ (babu, “female servant”, literally “mother”), from Old Javanese babu (“mother; older servant”) (cf. wawuh (“familiar, acquainted”)). Compare Portuguese babo.

parole.significato: a unit of measure for area on Java, equivalent to about 0.7 hectare; a portion of agricultural land of this size
dukun, a Javan or Malay witch doctor or folk healer
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese dukun or Malay dukun.

parole.significato: a soup made with beef or goat tripe and coconut milk, eaten with compressed rice cakes
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese gule, from Old Javanese gulay, probably from Tamil குழை (kuḻai, “to become soft, well cooked”).
Borrowed from Javanese ꦏꦭꦶ (kali), from Old Javanese kali, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kali.

parole.significato: a garden in the Dutch East Indies
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese ꦏꦼꦧꦺꦴꦤ꧀ (kebon). In the sense “gardener” a shortening from tukang kebun.

parole.significato: kris (Indonesian or Malay with a wavy blade)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese ꦏꦼꦫꦶꦱ꧀ (keris), from Old Javanese kĕris, kris.

parole.significato: prawn crackers, or any other deep-fried crackers from Indonesian (Javanese) cuisine
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese ꦏꦿꦸꦥꦸꦏ꧀ (krupuk), from Old Javanese kurupuk (“a crunchy flake”). Compare to Malay keropok, Indonesian kerupuk, and Tagalog kropek.

parole.significato: the activity of reading a text aloud to an audience in the evening in a singsong voice
palace or residence of an Indonesian native ruler
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese ꦥꦸꦫꦶ (puri, “palace”), Malay puri (“palace”), from Old Javanese purī, from Sanskrit पुरी (purī).

parole.significato: the traditional Indonesian (originally Javanese) salad dish consist of fruits and vegetables
parole.testo: From Javanese ꦫꦸꦗꦏ꧀ (rujak), from Old Javanese rujāk.

parole.significato: a sjambok, a long heavy whip
parole.testo: Borrowed from Javanese cambuk or Malay cambuk, ultimately from Persian چابک (čâbok).

parole.significato: mung bean sprout(s), shoots of the mung bean
sea hibiscus, cottonwood hibiscus (Talipariti tiliaceum, syn. Hibiscus tiliaceus)
parole.testo: Compound of waroe (“sea hibiscus”) + boom (“tree”). The first element is borrowed from Javanese waru.
